newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Stork says Fokker pull-out talk premature.
newsitem.headline: Stork says Fokker pull-out talk premature.

text.p: Dutch engineering group Stork NV said on Monday media reports that it had pulled out of rescue talks for bankrupt planemaker Fokker were "premature" although it admitted there were problems.
"There are problems of a financial nature (with the rescue talks) but it's too early to comment on them," a Stork spokesman told Reuters.
Dutch newspaper De Telegraaf on Saturday cited sources close to the negotiations saying Stork had withdrawn because the Malaysian government had refused to help finance Fokker's start-up costs.
The Stork spokesman confirmed the company was reviewing its options and said it might make a further announcement soon.

A team from the Malaysian state investment company Khazanah visited the Netherlands last month to discuss a rescue plan for Fokker, which has been run by court-appointed insolvency lawyers since it was declared bankrupt over a year ago.

The Stork spokesman also denied a report in Monday's Volkskrant newpaper, which suggested other European aircraft makers, including Airbus Industrie, had put pressure on Stork to pull out of the negotiations.
"That's not true at all, there are no problems with Airbus," he said.
Fokker was forced into bankruptcy last year when majority shareholder Daimler Benz AG of Germany pulled the plug, saying it could no longer bear Fokker's huge losses.
The "Malaysian option" was seen as the final lifeline for one of the pioneering companies of European aviation.
But Dutch Economics Minister Hans Wijers last month warned against over-optimism, saying there would be no relaunch unless substantial foreign investment could be secured.
After Daimler abandoned Fokker, Stork bought the profitable Fokker aircraft maintenance and components businesses in a deal binding it to some degree of involvement in a relaunch.
